cases.sentence: ___ эта так понравилась ему, что он несколько раз принимался косить.
cases.translation: He liked this work so much that he took it up several times.
cases.explain: Работа is the subject of понравилась (pleased), so it stands in the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Взял у ___ косу и стал косить.
cases.translation: He took a scythe from a peasant and began to mow.
cases.explain: The preposition у (from/at) governs the genitive case.

cases.sentence: Да мою косу пошлите, пожалуйста, к ___, чтобы он отбил и вынес завтра.
cases.translation: Please send my scythe to Tit, so he can sharpen and bring it out tomorrow.
cases.explain: The preposition к (to) governs the dative case.

cases.sentence: Взял у мужика ___ и стал косить.
cases.translation: He took a scythe from a peasant and began to mow.
cases.explain: Косу is the direct object of the transitive verb взял (took), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.sentence: Личное дело, занимавшее Левина во время разговора его с ___, было следующее.
cases.translation: The personal matter occupying Levin during his conversation with his brother was as follows.
cases.explain: The preposition с (with) governs the instrumental case.

cases.sentence: Со времени приезда брата он был в ___, косить или нет.
cases.translation: Since his brother's arrival he had been in doubt, whether to mow or not.
cases.explain: The preposition в (in) governs the prepositional case here, even though this neuter noun's prepositional form coincides with its nominative.

reading.ru: В прошлом году, приехав однажды на покос и рассердившись на приказчика, Левин употребил свое средство успокоения.
reading.question: What did Levin do last year to calm himself after getting angry at the steward?
options: He went to the hayfield and started mowing
He went for a walk in the forest
He wrote a letter of complaint
reading.correct: He went to the hayfield and started mowing
reading.explain: The text says he used his means of calming down: taking a scythe from a peasant and beginning to mow.

reading.ru: Выкосил весь луг пред домом, и нынешний год с самой весны составил себе план — косить с мужиками целые дни.
reading.question: What plan did Levin make for this year, from early spring?
options: To mow together with the peasants for whole days
To hire more workers instead of mowing himself
reading.correct: To mow together with the peasants for whole days
reading.explain: The text says he made a plan from early spring to mow with the peasants for whole days.

reading.ru: «Нужно физическое движение, а то мой характер решительно портится», — подумал он, и решился косить, как ненеловко ему будет перед братом и народом.
reading.question: Why did Levin think he needed physical exercise?
options: Because otherwise his temper was decidedly worsening
reading.correct: Because otherwise his temper was decidedly worsening
reading.explain: Levin thought 'I need physical movement, or my character will decidedly get worse.'

reading.question: How did the steward react when told Levin might mow himself?
options: He refused to prepare the scythe
reading.explain: The text says the steward smiled and said 'Слушаюсь' (Yes, sir).

reading.ru: «Я очень люблю эту работу», — сказал Сергей Иванович.
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich say about mowing work?
options: That he loved this work very much
That he had never tried it
That it was beneath a gentleman
reading.correct: That he loved this work very much
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich says, 'I very much love this work.'

reading.ru: Сергей Иванович поднял голову и с любопытством посмотрел на брата.
reading.question: How did Sergei Ivanovich react when Levin said he wanted to mow a whole day with the peasants?
options: He raised his head and looked at his brother with curiosity
He immediately agreed to join him
reading.correct: He raised his head and looked at his brother with curiosity
reading.explain: The text says Sergei Ivanovich raised his head and looked at his brother with curiosity.

reading.ru: «Это прекрасно, как физическое упражнение, только едва ли можешь это выдержать, без всякой насмешки», — сказал Сергей Иванович.
reading.question: What doubt did Sergei Ivanovich express about Levin's plan?
options: That Levin could hardly endure it, though it was excellent exercise
That mowing was a waste of time
That the peasants would refuse to work with him
That the weather would not permit it
reading.correct: That Levin could hardly endure it, though it was excellent exercise
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich says it's excellent as physical exercise, but Levin could hardly stand it.

reading.ru: Но скажи, как мужики смотрят на это?
reading.question: What did Sergei Ivanovich ask about the peasants' view of Levin mowing?
reading.explain: Sergei Ivanovich asks, 'But tell me, how do the peasants look at this?'

reading.ru: На другое утро Константин Левин встал раньше обыкновенного, но хозяйственные распоряжения задержали его, и когда он приехал на покос, косцы шли уже по второму ряду.
reading.question: When Levin arrived at the hayfield the next morning, where were the mowers already?
reading.explain: The text says household duties delayed him, and when he arrived the mowers were already on their second row.

reading.ru: Он насчитал их сорок два человека.
reading.question: How many mowers did Levin count?
reading.explain: The text says he counted forty-two men.

reading.ru: Левин слез с лошади и, привязав ее у дороги, сошелся с Титом, который, достав из куста вторую косу, подал ее.
reading.question: What did Levin do after dismounting his horse?
options: He tied it by the road and met Tit, who handed him a second scythe from the bushes
He rode straight into the field on horseback
He sent the horse back home
He gave the horse to Tit to hold
reading.correct: He tied it by the road and met Tit, who handed him a second scythe from the bushes
reading.explain: Levin got off his horse, tied it by the road, and joined Tit, who produced a second scythe from the bushes and handed it to him.

reading.ru: Левин взял косу и стал примериваться.
reading.question: What did Levin do after taking the scythe from Tit?
options: He began to try it out, getting the feel of it
He immediately began mowing at full speed
He put it down and rested
He gave it back, saying he changed his mind
reading.correct: He began to try it out, getting the feel of it
reading.explain: The text says Levin took the scythe and began to try its feel.

reading.ru: Трава была низкая, придорожная, и Левин, давно не косивший и смущенный обращенными на себя взглядами, в первые минуты косил дурно, хотя и махал сильно.
reading.question: How did Levin mow in the first minutes?
options: Badly, though swinging hard, because he was out of practice and embarrassed by the watching eyes
He mowed faster than Tit from the start
reading.correct: Badly, though swinging hard, because he was out of practice and embarrassed by the watching eyes
reading.explain: The text says he mowed poorly in the first minutes, though swinging hard, being out of practice and self-conscious.

reading.ru: Тит все шел, не останавливаясь, не выказывая ни малейшей усталости.
reading.question: How did Tit continue mowing?
options: Without stopping, showing not the slightest fatigue
He gave up and sat down
reading.correct: Without stopping, showing not the slightest fatigue
reading.explain: The text says Tit kept going without stopping, showing not the least fatigue.

reading.ru: Но в это самое время Тит сам остановился и, нагнувшись, взял травы, отер косу и стал точить.
reading.question: What did Tit do just as Levin was about to ask him to stop?
options: Tit himself stopped, bent down, wiped his scythe with grass, and began sharpening it
Tit ordered Levin to stop instead
Tit walked away without a word
reading.correct: Tit himself stopped, bent down, wiped his scythe with grass, and began sharpening it
reading.explain: Just as Levin was about to ask him to stop, Tit himself stopped and began to sharpen his scythe.

reading.ru: Несмотря на то, что пот катил градом по его лицу и капал с носа, и вся спина его была мокра, как вымоченная в воде, ему было очень хорошо.
reading.question: Despite the sweat pouring off him, how did Levin feel?
reading.explain: The text says that despite the sweat, he felt very good.

reading.ru: Одни мужики пошли к кафтанам и надели их, другие точно так же, как Левин, только радостно пожимали плечами под приятным освежением.
reading.question: How did some peasants, like Levin, react to the sudden rain?
options: They joyfully shrugged their shoulders under the refreshing rain instead of covering up
reading.correct: They joyfully shrugged their shoulders under the refreshing rain instead of covering up
reading.explain: The text says some, like Levin, just joyfully shrugged their shoulders under the pleasant coolness of the rain.

reading.ru: Напившись кофе, Левин уехал опять на покос, прежде чем Сергей Иванович успел одеться и выйти в столовую.
reading.question: What did Levin do after drinking his coffee?
options: He went back to the hayfield before Sergei Ivanovich even got dressed
He went to sleep for the rest of the day
He waited for his brother to join him
He decided not to mow anymore that day
reading.correct: He went back to the hayfield before Sergei Ivanovich even got dressed
reading.explain: The text says after drinking coffee, Levin went back to the hayfield before Sergei Ivanovich managed to dress and come to the dining room.
